newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha agrees to OSCE mission.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha agrees to OSCE mission.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday agreed to receive a mission from Europe's top security body led by former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, a spokeswoman for the body said.
"President Berisha has agreed to the mission. Vranitzky will arrive tomorrow (Saturday) morning," a spokeswoman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) told Reuters.
Vranitzky said on Wednesday Albanian officials had informed the OSCE that the visit was "not welcome", but he said then he execed to travel to Tirana in the next few days.

Vranitzky and his mission was scheduled to arrive by private plane at Tirana airport at 8:15 a.m. (0715 GMT) and to hold talks with Berisha at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), the OSCE spokeswoman said. The mission would leave Albania on Saturday evening.

The delegation was to include OSCE secretary-general Giancarlo Aragona, American Democratic Party Congressman Eliot Engel of New York, and officials from Denmark, Switzerland and Poland, representing the current, past and future chairmen of the 54-member state body. Russia and a troika of European Union states from the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Ireland would also be represented.
The OSCE mission was the latest in a series of international efforts to help broker a political settlement in Albania and to end a week-old rebellion in the south of the Balkan state.
